: 
This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for the relief of compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12%
p.a.
2.

The brief facts of case is as under:
That on 23.11.2022 at about 9.30 p.m. Lakshmamma N. was proceeding as a pillion rider on MVC No.7306/2022 3 SCCH 5 motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-EW-4985 which was rode by her husband Annegowda near House of Venkatesh, Mutturu Village, at that time, all of a sudden a dog came infront of the vehicle, due to the said impact, Lakshmamma fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, she was shifted to N.H.Hospital, Arekere, thereafter shifted to Neurobharat Hospital, Shimoga, wherein she took treatment as inpatient.
Further petitioners contended that, Lakshmamma was succumbed to the fatal injuries on 30.04.2023 and they have spent more than Rs.12,00,000/- towards medical and other expenses.
3. At the time of accident, deceased/ Lakshmamma N. was aged about 42 years, she was working as coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Petitioner No.1(A) and 1(B) are children of the deceased/Lakshmamma N.
With regard to the accident, crime No.537/2022 is registered against the rider of the MVC No.7306/2022 4 SCCH 5 said motor cycle before the Tunga Nagar Police Staation.
Respondent No.1 is R.C.Owner, respondent No.2 is insurer, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

Hence prays to allow the petition and grant compensation.
4.
On service of notice, respondent No.1/owner has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer has appeared and filed written statement.

Respondent No.2 submitted that, it has issued long term insurance policy to motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-14-EW-4985 from 13.10.2021 to 12.10.2026 and the risk of pillion rider covered for 1 year i.e., from 13.10.2021 to 12.10.2022 and the remaining period only the third party risk was covered.

Further alleged accident was occurred on 23.11.2022, as such the risk of the pillion rider was not covered under the policy, as the deceased was not a third party and no additional premium was collected to cover the risk of pillion rider.
MVC No.7306/2022 5 SCCH 5
Further respondent No.2 seeks protection under Sec.147 and Sec.149(2) of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.2 submitted that, there is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.

Respondent No.2 submitted that, there was lapse of 1 day in lodging the Lakshmamma.N vs Bharath S.K on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380123/
2 complaint.

Further submitted that, alleged accident was took place on 23.11.2022, however the deceased died on 30.04.2023 i.e., after lapse of 5 months from the date of accident and there was no nexus between the injuries and death caused to the deceased and death was not due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

Further submitted that, rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-14-EW- 4985 was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and also denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Further denied relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Accordingly prays to dismiss the petition.

Based on the pleadings of the parties this court has framed the following::
::RE-CASTED ISSUES::
1. Whether Petitioners prove that, Smt. Lakshmamma died due to grievous injuries sustained in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 23.11.2022 at about 9.30 a.m. near House of Venkatesh, Mutturu Village due to rash and negligent riding of rider motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 14-EW-4985 as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so how much and from whom?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, Petitioner No.1(A)/son of the deceased is examined as PW-1,
Dr.Satvik, Consultant Neurosurgeon at Neurobharat Hospital, Shimoga is examined as PW-2 and exhibited 14 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14.
On the other hand, Assistant Manager of respondent No.2 is examined as MVC No.7306/2022 7 SCCH 5 RW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.2A and closed evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record, and my findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 :
In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 :

As per final order for the  following:
 ::REASONS::
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1(A)/son of the deceased has deposed as PW-1.
In his chief-examination he has reiterated the facts narrated in his petition.

In this regard he has exhibited copy of FIR as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar with sketch Lakshmamma.N vs Bharath S.K on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380123/
3 as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report as Ex.P.4, copy of wound certificate as Ex.P.5, copy of charge sheet as Ex.P.6.
MVC No.7306/2022 8 SCCH 5 9.
Further petitioners have examined Dr.Satvik P.G. Consultant Neurosurgeon at Neurobharat Hospital as PW-2.

On perusal of evidence of PW-1, PW-2 and the records those were marked as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 corroborates the case of the petitioners about causing of the accident dated 23.11.2022 as alleged in the petition and in the evidence of PW-1.
10.

Per contra, the Assistant Manager of respondent No.2 Insurance Company is examined as RW-1 and marked authorization letter as Ex.R.1 and copy of policy as Ex.R.2. R.W-1 in his examination in chief not disputed about manner of accident and admitted about the policy to the offending vehicle.

It is the contention of respondent No.2 that it has issued long term policy valid from 13.10.2021 to12.10.2026 and the risk coverage for pillion rider is for 1 year i.e from 13.10.2021 to 12.10.2022 and for remaining period only third party risk is covered.
As on the date of accident the MVC No.7306/2022 9 SCCH 5 risk of pillion rider was not covered under the policy as she was not a third party.
Hence respondent No.2 is not liable to pay compensation.
11. On perusal cross examination of P.W-1(a) the involvement and manner of accident is not disputed.
As per version of P.W-1(a) both the riders of motor cycle were wearing helmet at the time of accident.
The death of Smt.Lakshmamma.N is admitted but the respondent No.2 taken specific contention that there is no nexus between accident and the death of Smt.Lakshmamma.N.
At this juncture it is relevant to refer the cross examination of P.W-2 wherein he stated that after partial recovery Smt.Lakshmamma.N was discharged from the hospital.
Further he stated that the cause of death of Smt. Lakshmamma.N is infection due to multiple injuries.
It is not the case of petitioner that prior to death Smt. Lakshmamma.N sustained injuries due to any other cause.
P.W-2 specifically stated that on 24.04.2023 MVC No.7306/2022 10 SCCH 5 Smt. Lakshmamma.N was discharged from the hospital and on 30.04.2023 Smt. Lakshmamma.N died.
The medical records shows that Smt. Lakshmamma.N was under continuous medical treatment for head injury.
Merely post mortem is not done it cannot held that death is not due to accidental injuries.

Learned counsel for petitioner relied on decision reported in i) 1994 ACJ1017,
ii) 2008 ACJ191, iii).2011 ACJ 2197 and decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.21548/2008 to contend the nexus between death and accidental injuries.

In MFA No.2218/2016 (MV-D) C/w. MFA Crob. No.16/2021 in the case of M/s. United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Smt. Mangamma and others to contend that wherein Hon'ble High court of Karnataka by considering continuous treatment taken by the injured and as there is nexus between accident and death granted compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further in MFA No.11237/2012 (MV) in the case of Suresh V/s.
Hanmanthu and another, wherein MVC No.7306/2022 11 SCCH 5 Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka reversed the finding of tribunal and held that as per the medical records injured has been under consistent medical treatment ever since the date of accident and there is a nexus between accident and death. There is no contrary evidence by respondent No.2 that death of Smt. Lakshmamma.N is due any other reason.

Thus the contention of respondent No.2 that there is no nexus between the Lakshmamma.N vs Bharath S.K on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380123/
4
death of Smt. Lakshmamma.N and accidental injuries is not proved.

12. The respondent No.2 relied on decision reported in ILR2013 KAR4519 in the case of Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.,Ltd., Vs. Mallappa Basappa Indur,by his Lrs and Another,Wherein the death of injured was after lapse of five years of accident and the appeal filed by Insurance company by challenging the award of tribunal was allowed.

entities.text: Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co.,Ltd., Vs. Mallappa Basappa Indur,by his Lrs and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand the petitioners proved that the death of Smt. Lakshmamma.N was due to bodily injuries sustained in road Traffic MVC No.7306/2022 12 SCCH 5 accident.

In the absence of rebuttal evidence it is proved by the the petitioners about death of N.Lakshmamma due to the accident occurred on 23.11.2022 at about 9.30 a.m. when she was proceeding as a pillion rider on motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-EW-4985 near House of Venkatesh, Mutturu Village.
In the absence of rebuttal evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioners.
13. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligence of the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14-EW-4985.

Under such circumstances,
considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the petitioners, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
14. Issue No.2:-
As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/N. Lakshmamma was aged about 42 years as MVC No.7306/2022 13 SCCH 5 on the date of accident.

For proof of age of the deceased,
petitioners have produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.7, wherein date of year of the deceased is mentioned as 1980 and alleged accident was occurred on 2022.

On considering Ex.P.7,
age of the deceased is considered about 42 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 14 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. As per the case of the petitioners, deceased was working as coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
In this regard, petitioners have not produced any documents.
Hence by relying upon the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Karnataka State Legal Services Authority Bengaluru, notional income of the petitioner is taken at the rate of Rs.15,500/- p.m.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Hence monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.15,500/- p.m.
the MVC No.7306/2022 14 SCCH 5 said fact is taken into consideration for the purpose of calculation of loss of dependency.
16. Further petitioner No.1(A) and 1(B) are sons of the deceased Lakshmamma N.
To prove the said fact, petitioners have furnished copy of aadhar cards marked as Ex.P.7, which reveals that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased/N.Lakshmamma.

17. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, the Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 25% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged in between 40 and 50 years, in case of fixed salary employee.

In the case on hand, the monthly income of the deceased is taken at the rate of Rs.19,375/- p.m. hence, which is taken for additional weightage at the rate of 25% with reference to Lakshmamma.N vs Bharath S.K on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380123/
5 her age.
MVC No.7306/2022 15 SCCH 5 18.
Hence, the following calculation is made for loss of dependency.
Sl. Particulars Calculation  No.

(i) Monthly Income Rs.15,500/-
 (ii) 25% of (i) above if added to Rs.15,500/- (+)
the monthly income as Rs.3,875/- = future prospects Rs.19,375/-
(iii) 1/3 of (ii) of the same to be Rs.19,375/(-) deducted towards personal Rs.6,458/- = and living expenses Rs.12,917/-p.m

Monthly income (iv) Compensation after Rs. 12,917x 12 x 14 multiplier of 14 is applied Total Rs.21,70,056/-
19.

As per judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi,in Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014, the loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be enhanced at the rate of 10 percent in every three years.

sentences.text: Therefore petitioner No.1(A) and 1(B) are entitled MVC No.7306/2022 16 SCCH 5 for Rs.48,000/- towards filial consortium.

Further petitioners also entitled for loss of estate of Rs.18,000/- and also they are entitled for funeral expenses for an amount of Rs.18,000/-.
20.

To prove the nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased Lakshmamma and treatment taken by her before death, petitioners have examined Dr.Satvik P.G., Consultant Neurosurgeon at Neurobharat Hospital as PW-2 and marked IP records as Ex.P.12, case sheets as Ex.P.13 and CT- Scans and X-ray Films as Ex.P.14.
Petitioners have furnished medical bills to the tune of Rs.9,77,120/-.

On perusal of said medical bills at Ex.P.11 Sl.No.358 to 368 i.e., for Rs.16,500/- are pertaining to ambulance bills as the author of said bill is not examined, the petitioners are not entitled for said bills of ambulance.
Regarding medical bills nothing is disputed during the cross examination of P.W-1(a).
Thus petitioners are entitled for medical bill.

The details of compensation awarded is as under:
Sl.No. Head of Compensation Amount/Rs.
1. Loss of dependency 21,70,056-00 2.
Loss of parental consortium 48,000-00 Lakshmamma.N vs Bharath S.K on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145380123/
6 3. Loss of Estate 18,000-00 4.
Funeral Expenses 18,000-00 5.
Medical Expenses 9,60,620-00 Total 32,14,676-00 21.
Accordingly this tribunal hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.32,14,676/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
22. The respondent No.2 taken contention that it has not collected the additional premium to cover the risk of pillion rider

and in this regard respondent No.2 relied on decision of Hon'ble High Court of Madras in CMA No.2093 of 2023, wherein by relying the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Oriental Insurance Co.
MVC No.7306/2022 18 SCCH 5 Ltd vs. Sudhakaran K.V (2008) 7 SCC 428 "25

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Co.
MVC No.7306/2022 18 SCCH 5 Ltd vs. Sudhakaran K.V (2008) 7 SCC 428
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The law which emerges from the said decision is:(i) the liability of the insurance company in the case of this nature is not extended to a pillion-rider of the motor vehicle unless the requisite amount of premium is paid for covering his/her risk

; (ii) the legal obligation arising under Section 147 of Act cannot be extended to an injury or death of owner of vehicle or the pillion -rider; (iii) the pillion-rider in a two wheeler was not to be treated as a third party when the accident has taken place owing to rash and negligent ridingof the scooter and not on the part of the driving of another vehicle,"

Further in CMA No.2093 of 2023, by relying the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mohana Krishnan.S Vs.K Balasubramaniyam in Special Leave to Appeal(C No. 3433 of 2020) held that "However, the current legal position is that pillion rider is not covered under third party insurance unless an additional premium in this regard was paid."
MVC No.7306/2022 19 SCCH 5 23.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the case on hand respondent No.2 during the evidence of R.W.1 produced Ex.R.2.
Admittedly the policy coverage for own damage is from 13.10.2021 to 12.10 2022 and for third party liability is from 13.10.2021 to 12.10.2026.
The date of accident is 23.11.2022.
There is no evidence regarding payment of additional premium to cover the risk of pillion rider.
Therefore respondent No.1 being the owner of motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-14- EW-4985 alone is liable to pay compensation.
Respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the award amount with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
24. Issue No.3:

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,14,676/- (Rupees Thirty two lakhs fourteen thousand six hundred seventy six Only) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.1 shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 50:50 in the award amount.

The petitioners are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
